stem:
Brandon drew the two congruent squares shown.

• He divided one square into 2 congruent triangular parts.
• He divided the other square into 2 congruent rectangular parts.

Which statement is true?

options.label: F
options.text: Each triangular part and each rectangular part represents \( \frac{1}{2} \) the area of one square.

options.label: G
options.text: Each triangular part has an area that is greater than the area of each rectangular part.

options.label: H
options.text: Each triangular part and each rectangular part represents \( \frac{1}{4} \) the area of one square.

options.label: J
options.text: Each rectangular part has an area that is greater than the area of each triangular part.

visual_elements: Two identical squares side by side, both unmarked.
difficulty_rationale: The problem involves recognizing that dividing congruent squares into two congruent parts results in equal area parts, a straightforward concept involving basic fraction knowledge.
